title: Remove K-Balanced Substrings
summary: Given a string s made of '(' and ')', and an integer k, repeatedly remove all non-overlapping k-balanced substrings (exactly k '(' followed by k ')') from s.
statement: Given a string s made of '(' and ')', and an integer k, repeatedly remove all non-overlapping k-balanced substrings (exactly k '(' followed by k ')') from s. Continue until no k-balanced substring remains. Return the final string. For example, with s = "(())" and k = 1, the process results in an empty string.
constraints: s has two to 100,000 parentheses and k is at most half its length.
Repeatedly remove every occurrence of exactly k opening parentheses followed by k closing parentheses.
Continue until no such substring remains and return the residual string.
hints: Only the final runs of equal parentheses can form a new removable block.
Compress the processed prefix into character/count runs and inspect the last two runs after each closing parenthesis.
When the closing run reaches k and the preceding opening run has at least k, delete both portions and discard empty runs.
All earlier runs were already stable; each deletion exposes precisely the new boundary that the same stack logic checks next.
editorial: All earlier runs were already stable; each deletion exposes precisely the new boundary that the same stack logic checks next.

tests.explanation: Removing the inner pair creates another pair, so repeated removal leaves the empty string.
The middle pair is removed and the remaining string is ((.
